law: #e12 ruling D11; close-gate item 5 (tier labels on original-language claims)
status: MEASURED TABLE, ROUTED FOR RATIFICATION. Not yet wired into a gate. The month-ordinal field is INFERRED from the construction's shape, and a false flag on a dateline would be expensive, so the controlling agent ratifies the table and the arm then keys off the ratified table rather than off this builder's positional rule.
why_three_fields_not_one: the ruling's ground truth is that MT 32:17 names no month. The verse CONTAINS the month word - it reads 'on the fifteenth of the month' - and what it lacks is the month ORDINAL. A detector keyed on the month word alone would have reported the controlling agent's own vector as a contradiction. The inventory separately documents that this word is a homograph trap in the other direction. So year term, month anchor and month ordinal are kept apart.

measured.date_phrase_skeleton: ויהי בשתי עשרה שנה בחמשה עשר לחדש

regression_vector_from_the_ruling.reading: year present, month anchor present, month ORDINAL absent - which is exactly what 'names no month' means and why the c15 challenge against a row's month claim stands

honest_limits: The ordinal stem list is hand-built and covers the ordinals Ezekiel's datelines actually use; an unlisted construction would read as 'no ordinal' and is the failure direction to watch.
Day numbers are not separated out as their own field: in this construction the day is the cardinal standing immediately before the month anchor, and it is visible in the skeleton rather than parsed.
Skeleton matching folds points and accents, so a homograph of the year or month word would match. The inventory's documented homograph cases are outside the 14 dateline verses.
Nothing here is wired into a gate and no row is scored by it.
